discovery: Discovery of quantized conductance in ballistic one-dimensional semiconductor constrictions
subfield: Condensed matter physics / mesoscopic semiconductor physics
motivation: In 1988 two independent teams, at Delft/Philips (van Wees et al.) and at Cambridge (Wharam, Pepper et al.), showed that the conductance of a narrow, gate-defined channel in a GaAs two-dimensional electron gas rises in steps of 2e^2/h. This was the first direct demonstration that electrical conduction through a nanoscale device is carried by discrete quantum modes, as Landauer had predicted. The result founded mesoscopic quantum transport. Quantum point contacts became the workhorse charge sensors and building blocks for quantum dots, spin qubits, electron quantum optics and single-electron devices, including today's semiconductor quantum processors. Later work on one-dimensional systems, such as the 0.7 anomaly and incipient Wigner crystallisation, revealed rich many-body physics. The discovery has been reproduced across many materials and remains a basic test of quantum electronics at the ultimate scale.
